svg.title: TOPAK D3 — The record planes: what is ordered, what is carried, what is kept, what is erased
svg.desc: Four stores hold the record. The Paxos log orders; Kafka carries, as transport only (ADR-0005, ratified Batch 27); the archive is the system of record; a separately governed store holds plaintext so it can be destroyed. A round's topic opens with the tool list, and its Actuate records carry labels. Across all four runs the plane boundary (B5): control-plane facts cross and survive, cognitive payloads are reduced to a hash and a pointer.
svg.text: TOPAK · D3

text.tspan: The record planes: what is ordered, what is carried, what is kept, what is erased

svg.text: Four stores hold the record. The Paxos log orders; Kafka carries, as transport only (ADR-0005, ratified Batch 27); the archive is the system of record; a separately governed store holds plaintext so it can be destroyed. A round's topic opens with the tool list, and its Actuate records carry labels. Across all four runs the plane boundary (B5): control-plane facts cross and survive, cognitive payloads are reduced to a hash and a pointer.
The ordering authority and the causal frame (ADR-0015; ADR-0005). Every effect has a
consensus-ordered, signed, authorizing predecessor here; the log index is the fence. Neither the
topic nor the emission is the record; the log is (ToO §4.4). No snapshots or compaction at the
reference (G14).
Every Entry, fourteen kinds at the rebuilt reference: Grant, Renew, Admit, EndRound, Revoke,
EpochIncrement, Contested, ProfileRegister, Issue, GatesPassed; since 2026.10.05 an
operator's signed Control, EmergencySeating (BOOTSTRAP) and Activate; and
BreakGlassApprove, retired and refused at apply (state.rs). Each carries an id
n<replica>-<boot>-<counter>, so a re-proposal applies once.
Admits are F1; a vote's admit is F3; stops are F2, an operator's three denies among them;
issuances F4; an activation and an emergency seat's calls F5; erasure events would be F6
(unbuilt).
A Consult admit carries the item's label and delivery mode; an Actuate admit its label facts
Denials are not here: a denial changes no state, so it is never proposed.
None. A payload appears only as a digest: Draft content, Emit/Report records, Invoke/
Actuate inputs, the frozen input (Admitted, state.rs).

text.tspan: Accepted · ADR-0005 · C4 · Batch 27 · built at reference

svg.text: Transport with a durability window (acks=all), neither ordering authority nor system of record
(ADR-0005 §1, ratified 2026.10.04 at R2). One single-partition topic per principal per epoch or
round, sealed, per-topic ACL, per-use retention, the unit of erasure (ADR-0003). The debt
ADR-0033 §2's K row carried since Batch 7 is discharged (G10 §1, item 5).
Every record's envelope: kind, seat, fence, the authorizing admit index, the per-lease sequence
number, the payload digest (headers topak-*).
The opening record first: the tool list, written by the mechanism at grant, with no admit and no
sequence number (ADR-0048 §2; ADR-0042 A1). Then the Actuate record of ADR-0042 §3,
now with four label fields; heartbeats; denial records (no admit, no sequence, with at and
decided_by) while the round is open; on an operator's topic, its control records; the seal
marker.
Written only after the admit commits; denials unordered, by the deciding replica.
Emit and Report bodies; an Actuate record's inputs and result themselves, in full whatever
was delivered to the principal, under the topic's ACL and in the round's unit of erasure
(ADR-0042 §3, A1; ADR-0047 §5). The tool list in the opening record's payload, and a task's
bytes, at the reference in the same record (ADR-0048 §2; ADR-0050 §5; ToO §7.10).
A vote's emission carries the vote and a hash-and-pointer to its commentary, not the
commentary (ToO §4.4).
Cognitive intermediate state (scratchpads, chains of thought) is never written to round topics
The system of record (ADR-0005 §1, Accepted; ADR-0004, Accepted, is scoped to it). Fed by its
own ETL per use case; not a tier of the topic: read under its own authority, it neither extends a
topic's life nor survives its erasure (ADR-0003 A3). The reference writes archive.jsonl per
replica, a projection of the log, which is not this archive (register G9).
The control-plane record keeps a hash and a pointer for every cognitive payload (ADR-0004).
Trace conformance needs actions, identities and ordering, not prompt text: the archive holds what
replay and conformance need (ADR-0004 Context).
Six forensic classes are non-erasable here for the declared horizon (ADR-0028).
None in plaintext: a hash and a pointer per payload.
Plaintext lives in a store built for deletion (ADR-0004). Its readers are where the replay-harness
attestation requirement attaches; the pointer to it is itself a disclosure (demand type 5, declined).
None: the store holds payloads only.
Its entries are reached by the archive's pointers, and erased by deleting them (ADR-0006).
Prompts, reasoning, review commentary: all erasable. No cognitive payload is in the forensic
floor (ADR-0028 §1).
B5 plane boundary · facts cross and survive; payloads are reduced to hash + pointer
emission after commit:
admit index, fence, seq
ETL per use case
(not built)
hash + pointer
(not built)

text.tspan: One round topic, from open to erased (ADR-0003; ADR-0021; ADR-0042 §5)

svg.text: Identity: topak.<chain>.<domain>.<seat>.e<epoch>.r<round>. The rules-epoch chain is part of the name (ADR-0003 A1): re-genesis restarts epochs and rounds at zero, and two development resets once wrote into the same Kafka topic (finding 4). A sealed topic is never written again.
Opens with the tool list: the mechanism's
opening record, written at grant before the
session exists; no admit, no seq, outside every
watermark (ADR-0048 §2).
Admitted emissions at seq 1, 2, …; Actuate
records; heartbeats.
Denials while open, unordered.
Run: when the lease ends: expiry, operator end,
epoch fence, targeted revocation, a new rules
epoch; not on renewal (ADR-0042 §5).
Build: at gate submission, the principal's topic
In-flight Actuate calls written unknown ahead of
the seal marker.
Denials under the round's lease once its topic is
sealed; never an emission.
Bounded: after_topic_limit (dev 64) per
deciding replica, since the counter is not
replicated (I23), then one overflow marker.
ADR-0003 A2 · confirmation-required C1.
Run: Run's horizon. Build: the production
lifetime of any artifact promoted from the round
One store for the whole retention: no tiered
storage (0003.7, scoped by A3).
Erasure drops the sealed topic and its after
companion, and the plaintext-store entries
(ADR-0006). No signature or hash chain is
edited.
Not built; genesis issues no erasure roster, so
X2-erasure admits nothing.

text.tspan: Accepted · C4 · A1, A2 at Batch 34

svg.text: The round topic, or its .after companion
The principal's seat
The lease's fence (log index of its grant)
open (the opening record), emit (an admitted Emit or Report), actuate, control (an operator's ordered request,
on its own topic), deny or overflow. The seal is a marker record with a topak-seal header whose reason is in
Rust's Debug form (Submitted), not the serde form (submitted) every other surface uses (inventory finding 14)
Log index of the authorizing Admit, or of the ordered Control; none for a denial or the opening record
Per-round sequence: emissions in Build, effect-bearing admits in Run (ADR-0042 §2); none for a denial, a control
record or the opening record
Digest of the payload in canonical JSON. The Kafka value itself is not canonical (serde_json::to_vec), so a
reader re-canonicalizes to check it (inventory finding 13)
The record itself: cognitive payload for an emission; for a denial {denied, reason, epoch, round, at,
decided_by} with content as digests; for the overflow marker {overflow, limit, epoch, round, at,
decided_by}; for the opening record {tool_list, task}; for a control record {control, sig, facts}

text.tspan: The round's opening record (ADR-0048 §2; ADR-0042 A1)

svg.text: open: written by the mechanism at grant, before the session exists, so nothing the principal does precedes it. The
principal cannot write it. If it cannot be written, no session is opened (I45)
None: it is not an effect, so it has no sequence number and is outside what a watermark covers; the mark does
not assert it was read (ADR-0043 §4 A1)
Digest of the rendered tool list; the bundle revision is in the list (ADR-0042 A1)
The list itself: the interface of every entry of the lease's revision the lease may call, in the mechanism's fixed form;
and the round's task where the grant carried one (ADR-0050 §5). A renewal writes none: the bundle is fixed across
renewal (ADR-0031 R2)
The principal's seat and the lease's fence
Control plane
The log index at which the admit committed
Control plane
The sequence number of §2
Control plane
Name and digest of the allowlist entry
Control plane
Was: whether the admit was under X1. Replaced by seatKind (A2): with X1
retired no admit is under it
The kind of the seat that made the call; a call by an emergency seat is what a
reader looks for where it looked for breakGlass. The activation is the F5 record
(ADR-0042 A2; provisional with ADR-0052)
Control plane
Digest of the inputs
Control plane
returned, failed or unknown
Control plane
Digest of what the tool returned, when it returned
Control plane
The label of each input that is a handle (A1; ADR-0047 §5)
Control plane
The result's label after the join of ADR-0047 §1
Control plane
clear or handle: how the result reached the principal
Control plane
The labels of everything delivered clear to the principal in the round, as it stood
when the call was admitted (ADR-0047 §4)
Control plane
{kind, target} a hosted Wasm tool was held to: its entry's declaration in the
lease's revision. Reference only: not a field of ADR-0042 §3 (I44)
Control plane
The inputs and the result themselves, in full whatever delivery says:
suppressed to the Thinker is not suppressed to the Observer (ADR-0047 §5)

text.tspan: ADR-0003, clause by clause (clause annotation C1, with A1–A3)

svg.text: Topic per principal per epoch/round
No
Core; 0003.2 and 0003.3 have no meaning without it
A topic is identified by its rules-epoch chain as well as by principal and epoch/round
Ratified 2026.09.25 (Batch 5); not confirmation-required. Finding 4
Sealed on emit completion
No
Core; defines the unit of erasure
One companion topic, after, for denials after the seal: never an emission, same ACL and retention, dropped
with the round; bounded, with a marker
Ratified 2026.09.25 (Batch 5); confirmation-required C1. Finding 11
Per-topic ACL model
No
Follows from 0003.1
Retention scoping
Entangled with the open raw-emission retention question (0003 vs 0006). Likely first to be superseded
Replay authorization
Overlaps ADR-0020: authorization to replay and the scope of replay are different decisions
Wrapper-Rego masking
Confirmed independently supersedable. Not built at the reference
No tiered storage
Operational; a degeneracy candidate under ADR-0023
No tiered storage is one store for a topic's whole retention, not a retention length; the archive is not a tier
Ratified 2026.09.30 (Batch 17) as a scoping, not a reversal
Separate read-only principals for audit; archive is its own ETL per use case
Carry no clause number (S3-2)
The Paxos log. An effect is an admit (ADR-0015), and an admit has one position in the log
The transport. A topic's offsets order one principal's round and nothing across rounds or principals (ADR-0003)
The archive (ADR-0004), with its governed plaintext store and the forensic horizon
The transport. Retention is per use case and a round's topic is the unit of erasure, so what it holds is not durable in the
sense a record needs
Kafka, at the reference: durability within the window (acks=all), delivery to the readers in W(p)
The K in TOPAK names the transport role; ordering and record-keeping are not asked of it (ADR-0045 T-0045-5, delegated). No vector clock is designed, and none is owed (R1).
The log index

text.tspan: A principal's effects within a round

svg.text: The sequence number, assigned when the admit is applied, so every replica assigns the same one
ADR-0042 §2 for Run; ADR-0039 §1
The log index and sequence number it carries. It is written only after its admit commits, so the topic never holds an emission the log does not order
ADR-0033 §2, K row
Nothing. It is written by the deciding replica, unordered, while the topic is open and to the after companion once it is sealed
Not the frame at all: causality orders events and bounds no interval

A reader orders a topic by the numbers its records carry, not by their offsets: offsets are evidence of arrival only. Denials are the remaining gap: a sequence number on denials is open (item 44, as at G9). ADR-0051 §5 (Proposed) would answer it without one: a denial record's at, the log index the
deciding replica had applied, and decided_by, which the reference already writes, made part of its schema.
The authoritative vote is the admit decision in the log, which F3 retains.
The voter's round-topic emission carries the vote together with a hash-and-pointer to its commentary in the separately governed store; the commentary is what erasure removes.
Without the split the record contradicts itself: a topic holding vote and commentary is either erasable as a unit, losing F3, or unerasable, losing the commentary's erasability.
A Build round is one pipeline invocation; each seat holds its own topic, sealed when the artifact is submitted to the gate (§3).
Every vote covers artifact digest ∧ sealed topic-set digest (§4): voters sign provenance, not only the product.
Retained for the production lifetime of any artifact promoted from the round (§7); the topic stays the unit of erasure.

text.tspan: Replay reconstructs what crossed the membrane (ADR-0020)

svg.text: The replayable record of a round: actions attempted, including those denied; effects emitted; lease and epoch transitions; the Persona binding in force.
The Observer and replay read the same stream: no privileged channel, so detection latency L stays an honest number.
Root-cause analysis can establish what a principal did, never why.

text.tspan: Ordering across topics comes from the log (ToO §4.2; ADR-0005 §2)

svg.text: Within-partition order gives no global timeline once there is a topic per round. An emission carries the admit's log index, the fence and a per-lease sequence number, which closes ADR-0015's one residual:
effects admitted in a round and emitted at different times (G15).
The quarantine-gate question no longer gates ADR-0005 and stays open on its own account (ADR-0005 §3; ADR-0039 finding 1).

text.tspan: Who reads a round topic, and what gates the read

svg.text: W(p): the principal's cell Observer and its domain's correlators (ADR-0038 §2). An Observer is given its Thinker's tool list by reading the opening record (ADR-0043 §4 A1).
Operators read each other's topics, where every control action is written (ADR-0050 §6), and an emergency seat's topic (ADR-0052 §4): both provisional.
At the reference nothing gates a read: the mechanism has no read path for topics, so who may read one is the transport's configuration. Operators and emergency seats add readers that nothing gates

text.tspan: A lineage reads the opening record (ADR-0035 R5, R6)
Proposed · ADR-0035, with R4 to R7

svg.text: A round's tool list is ingress and consumed: it enters both sets as the object the opening record's digest names, and, shared by every lineage under one bundle, it can only move a pair toward refusal
An item delivered as a handle is ingress and not consumed (R5). It applies to no lineage node today: Build's Read is not labelled.
R7: an operator's lineage is declared, rooted in its identity provider.
It leaves a verifying envelope over unreadable ciphertext, a hole no auditor can tell from suppression (ADR-0003 Context; ToO §4.3).
Erasure is deletion of sealed topics and of plaintext-store entries (ADR-0006).
Topic count scales with principals × rounds: broker metadata pressure needs a lifecycle story.
A masking miss has a blast radius of one round. Re-genesis migration of read access is open (G17).
